institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Due to me considering taking my entire master at the destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: At first it was a bit difficult, but as soon as you were on the right track and got help it got a lot easier. Generally a lot of the information was not really needed since i am a scandic student and was abroad in scandinavia

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help and information at the key help desk. An entire two weeks ish of exchange student activities and information presentations, both social and practical.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: extremely easy the host institution had their own housing so i just applied and got housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: All places at my host university was off campus so i dont think it applies for my

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a few wierd things i thought when talking to other student. Not getting certaint courses allowed even though another student with same study program was allowed the same course. The main problem was getting courses allowed from both my own and host university

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: sending an email with the courses i was allowed to take through my OLA, then i was signed up for all the courses i was allowed to take, so i went and resigned from the courses i did not want, since i was registered for too many courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email conversations with the erasmus student coordinator at my host university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Moderately, some of the courses i would have liked were spot limited which was the reason i did not get them other wise kind of sucxcessfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure the Online learning Agreement is number one priority

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Was a bit lower than i expected. But i think is was due to my hopes of what i was going to learn, as well as two of my courses being fairly easy. One of them was a course in norwegian that was mandatory for the host university's biotechnology bachelor students, this course should probably not be an option for exchange students unless it is changed, due to it being mainly revision and article work. The other course was very short due to the teacher being away on field work so it was cut down

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty, similar with the programme of lectures followed by theoretical excercises and lab/group work

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIO-2606 General and marine biotechnology
KJE-2004 Bioinformatics - An introduction
SOA-1006 Arctic Norway - Aspects of Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If i am being completely honest none of them. I mean arctic norway was fun if you are interested and a lot of exchange student took it, so that was quite fun, but i was very short. Bioinformatics was a mandatory course for me it was pretty fun but i would have chosen something else if i could. Marine biotechnology, i really hoped would be fun and interesting, but lacked a lot of what i thought the course was going to be. It was mainly repetition and article work for the UiT Biotech bachelor student, which i already done a lot off. Though it was fun seeing all the repetition in the aspect of the marine sector, but this probably shouldnt be for exchange students

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The housing a UiT doesnt come fully equipped and you cant buy a start package. So the first week you need to buy sleeping gear, kitchen gear, blinds/curtains and so on

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food more expensive (cheaper if you prepare yourself and look at offers) personal item were cheaper, like outdoor equipment. Alcohol was very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All most any athletic sports club you could think of was there as a student team. The student bar/house held weekly activities. Gerenally a lot of activities and very good activities by the host university, university sport facility and housing facility. examples: waffle tuesday and friday, burger meal friday offer, colour run and so on

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going on trips with DNT-youth a norwegian trekking group for young people from 13-25, just check that is your age group

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All or as much of the nearby nature and wildlife that Tromsø has to offer. Don't be shy renting cars to go on trips. That is the best part of my exchange

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very very easy as a danish to adjust to norwegian culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do as much of the host university's recommendation in the start and try as many different sports as possible

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation for nature and hiking

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If You are going to take the train buy the ERASMUS+ interail ticket. I didnt get any information about it i was just lucky i knew someone who did earlier on their exchange. It is by far the cheapest way to get there by train possibly cheapest period. Enjoy go on hikes all the time if possible, it is fun having others to join you but if they dont just go yourself, it is so worth it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seek accommodation early before the host university recognises you as an official student

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The trips, the experience and the friends i made along the way

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friend and feeling lonely

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
